evidence.curator_note: The SLOW branch: a vertical DOUBLE-HEADED arrow under the molecular ion, labelled 'rH' on one side and 'slow' on the other. It is drawn as an equilibrium and is encoded with reversible=true, as are the four isomerisations that follow -- the schema's `reversible` flag is what lets this scheme be recorded as the book draws it rather than silently linearised into one-way steps. A C5 hydrogen (map 11) moves to the carbonyl oxygen, giving the distonic ion the page draws at the left of the second row: a neutral OH, a '+' printed on C2 and the radical dot on C5. *** Equation 9.27 draws NO CURVED ARROWS AT ALL -- not one, anywhere on the page. *** Every transformation is conveyed by a reaction-type label ('fast', 'slow', rH, rC) plus the changed structure. Book draws 0 arc(s) for this step and ALL of its electron moves are therefore curator-supplied. This is still a mechanism and not a bare result (contrast eq 9.5, which is in NON_MECHANISM_EQS): the page prints six successive INTERMEDIATE structures with explicit, individually localised charge and radical sites, and each consecutive pair differs by exactly one well-defined change, so the flow is recoverable without inventing connectivity. The book prints its OWN carbon numbers 1-6 on every structure, and this record reuses them as atom maps so the mapping can be checked against the page by eye. That numbering is the whole point of the equation: it is what distinguishes the fast route (which expels the C-1 methyl) from the slow one (which expels C-4 or C-6 after skeletal scrambling). Four curator-supplied moves: <1,2> build the new O-H bond from one C5-H electron plus the oxygen's odd electron, <3> leaves the second C5-H electron on C5 as the new radical, and <4> localises the C2=O pi PAIR onto oxygen, which is what neutralises the oxygen and puts the '+' on C2 exactly where the page prints it. MS CONTEXT: this route is metastable, not 70 eV -- the prose introduces it with 'Decompositions of low-energy, particularly metastable, ketone ions follow different pathways than those observed in the normal electron-impact-mass spectra', so activation_method is 'metastable-ion (MI) decomposition' and electron_energy_ev is null. MEASUREMENTS (convention F): this equation prints NO m/z value and no percentage anywhere -- not on the molecular ion, not on any intermediate, not on any product. Every mass in this record is CURATOR-COMPUTED from the instantiated structures. The ions are nevertheless marked detected=true with status 'proposed', following the corpus precedent of IMS8-EQ8.60 / IMS8-EQ8.81a/b, because the running prose reports them as observed species ('the 2-hexanone ion loses predominantly the C-1 methyl to give the stable acyl ion C4H9CO+'; 'protonated pentenone'). No relative_intensity is recorded: the only number on the page is the prose '<3%', which is an UPPER BOUND on a metastable branching ratio, not a 70 eV EI abundance.

Equilibrium arrow labelled 'rC': a genuine CARBON-SKELETON rearrangement, and the structures confirm the label. In the left-hand structure the chain runs C2-C3-C4-C5(.)-C6; in the right-hand one C3 is bonded directly to C5, C4 has become a pendant CH2. on C5, and the radical has moved from C5 to C4. That is a 1,2-alkyl shift. Book draws 0 arc(s); the three curator-supplied moves are the radical-shift triple: <1> one electron of the migrating C3-C4 bond into the forming C3-C5 bond, <2> the C5 radical completing that bond, <3> the other C3-C4 electron staying on C4 as the new radical site.

Equilibrium arrow labelled 'rH'. The hydroxyl hydrogen (map 11, the one that came off C5 two steps earlier) moves onto the C4 radical, converting it to a methyl and restoring a normal ionised ketone: the page draws the resulting structure with '+.' back on the oxygen, an explicit H on C5, and methyls numbered 4 and 6 -- i.e. the 4-methyl-2-pentanone molecular ion, a SKELETAL ISOMER of the substrate. This is the pivot of the whole equation: the carbon that will eventually be lost is no longer C1. Book draws 0 arc(s); the four moves are the reverse of the S1->S2 set -- <1,2> build the C4-H bond from one O-H electron plus the C4 radical, <3> leaves the other O-H electron on oxygen as its odd electron, and <4> returns an oxygen lone PAIR to the C2-O bond to re-form the C=O double bond and move the '+' back to oxygen.

Equilibrium arrow labelled 'rH', wrapping from the end of the second row to the start of the third. The remaining C5 hydrogen (map 13) moves to the oxygen, leaving a TERTIARY radical on C5 -- the page draws it with the dot on the carbon carrying both numbered methyls (4 and 6) -- with the '+' again on C2 and a neutral OH. Identical move set to step 1 of this record, with map 13 in place of map 11. Book draws 0 arc(s).

*** LABEL / DRAWING DISCREPANCY, recorded rather than resolved. *** The page labels this equilibrium 'rC', but the two structures it connects have the SAME carbon skeleton: both are C1-C2-C3-C5 with methyls 4 and 6 on C5, verified atom by atom at native resolution (left: OH and '+' on C2, explicit H on C3, radical on the C5 bearing both methyls; right: 'HO' with '+.', a C2=C3 double bond, and an H on that same C5). No bond between carbons is made or broken. What actually changes is a HYDROGEN: map 12 moves from C3 to C5, a C2=C3 pi bond forms, and the charge and odd electron end up together on oxygen. The step is therefore encoded as step_class 'hydrogen_rearrangement', following the DRAWN structures per convention A, and the book's 'rC' label is reported here rather than followed. (By contrast the earlier 'rC' at the start of row two IS a skeletal shift, so the notation itself is used consistently elsewhere -- which is what makes this instance look like a slip in the figure.) Book draws 0 arc(s); four curator-supplied moves: <1,2> build the C5-H bond from one C3-H electron plus the C5 radical, <3> puts the other C3-H electron into the forming C2=C3 pi bond, and <4> completes that pi bond with ONE electron from an oxygen lone pair -- which is precisely what leaves the oxygen with both the '+' and the odd electron the page prints on it.

Terminal branch, the UPPER of the two arrows leaving the ionised enol, labelled '- CH3.' with a '4' printed above it to say WHICH methyl is lost. The product is drawn as a hydroxy-substituted allylic cation -- an OH, a chain, and a '+' printed over a CURVE spanning three atoms to mark delocalisation -- i.e. protonated pentenone, the ion the prose names. LOCALIZATION (convention C): the delocalised drawing is stored as the single localised form C2=C3 with the '+' on C5, which is what these arrows produce; its partner is the C2(+)-OH / C3=C5 form. Book draws 0 arc(s); two curator-supplied moves, the same pairing pattern the i steps of IMS9-EQ9.25d/e use: one electron of the breaking C4-C5 bond leaves with the methyl radical <1> and the other travels through the conjugated system to the oxygen <2>, pairing with its odd electron so the product is an even-electron cation with a neutral OH. The gate reports '(soft) ... consistent with a lone pair rather than radicals' for exactly that pairing. NOTE: this ion and the fast route's acylium (IMS9-EQ9.27a) are BOTH C5H9O+ and therefore both m/z 85.0648 -- isomers, indistinguishable by mass, which is precisely why the book resorts to numbering the carbons to tell the two pathways apart.
